bash.message: Port 5005 is the dev backend, which talks to the REAL Neon database. Never curl/seed against it. Use the isolated e2e backend on 5006 (frontend/e2e, postgres-test).
That is the real Neon database. Do not connect to it from here; ask Nave to run it himself.
Only the isolated test DB (localhost:5433) may be opened with a SQL client.
Prisma writes/Studio must target the test DB: use `npm run schema:test:push`, or `dotenv -e .env.test -- prisma …`. `db push` on Neon needs Nave's explicit go-ahead and is run by him.
`.env` files hold real secrets (Neon URL, API keys). Do not read or copy them; `.env.example` / `.env.test.example` are fine.
This reads the REAL Neon schema (read-only) using backend/.env. It is meant to be run by Nave himself (deploy.sh runs it); confirm before running it from here.
Deploy goes to production (and pre-checks the live DB schema). Only with Nave's explicit go-ahead in this session.
This deletes the postgres-test data volume (test data only, but it also wipes the schema; it is rebuilt by `npm run schema:test:push`).

watch.message: Schema changed. Checklist: (1) the test DB is updated by `npm run schema:test:push` (also runs automatically before `npm run test:e2e`); (2) a new @default on an existing table silently reclassifies old rows under db push — plan a backfill; (3) Neon is NOT updated by deploy: `db push` there needs Nave's approval, and `npm run schema:check:prod` (run by Nave, read-only) will fail the deploy until it is done; (4) restart the backend container after a schema change.
Deploy configuration changed. Keep the schema gate (`schema:check:prod`) before any `fly deploy` in deploy.sh.
